chunks: Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh al-Barqī, from al-Qāsim ibn Yaḥyā, from his grandfather al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, from his father, from his forefathers, from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, who said:
When one of you undresses, al-Shayṭān looks at him and becomes desirous concerning him, so cover yourselves.

key_terms.الشَّيْطَانُ: Satan; the evil being who seeks to tempt and harm
key_terms.تَعَرَّى: to remove one's clothes; to become uncovered
key_terms.فَاسْتَتِرُوا: so conceal yourselves; keep yourselves covered
key_terms.فَطَمِعَ: then he becomes desirous or covetous; seeks an opportunity

ai.seo_question: Why does the hadith instruct a person to cover himself when undressing?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs believers to maintain covering when undressing, linking modest concealment with protection from al-Shayṭān. It conveys an ethical and practical etiquette, especially relevant to settings such as the bathhouse.
